title: KV economics orchestrator: hit-rate forecaster, TTL gradualizer, and key canonization spec
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Objective: Deliver an automated recommendation engine and safe-apply workflow that suggests per-prefix TTLs, cache key canonicalization rules, and batching-aware prefetch policies to minimize serving cost without violating latency SLOs. This ticket covers: hit-rate forecasting models, TTL gradualizer and rollback policy, canonical key derivation rules, simulation harness, and integration with Console rollout controls.

Motivation: Current manual TTL tuning causes over-retention and wasted GPU cycles. We need an orchestrator that uses workload-aware economics to propose conservative updates and run canaries/shadow probes before global application. Must support gradual apply with automatic rollback triggers tied to latency and hit-rate regressions.

Scope:
- Hit-rate forecaster: lightweight time-series and sample-based estimator per-prefix, accounting for prefix affinity and sequence-length buckets.
- TTL gradualizer: staged TTL increase/decrease policy with step sizes, cool-down windows, and safe gas limit to prevent cascade misses.
- Key canonization spec: deterministic rules to normalize variable tokens, collapse user-tokens for opt-in prefixes, and safe exceptions when user-level affinity is required.
- Prefetch policy suggestions: batching-aware prefetch thresholds for long-running chats where KV cache saves compute.
- Simulation harness: offline replay and counterfactual cost model to estimate cost delta and hit-rate change per suggestion.
- Safe-apply playbook: probing canary, shadow trial, staged rollout, rollback thresholds, and post-mortem checklist.

Success metrics:
- 8-15% reduction in token compute cost for targeted workloads within 30 days of rollout.
- No more than 1% tail-latency regressions (>99.9th p50 baseline) during staged apply.
- Tools produce actionable recommendations for 80% of high-volume prefixes identified by the profiler.

Out of scope: Automated forced de-duplication of user content within models (requires product sign-off) and on-prem specific packaging (handled in separate Private deployment ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation engine produces TTL suggestions for at least 100 prefixes from production sample and exposes confidence score.
Offline simulator produces estimated cost delta and hit-rate delta for each suggestion with synthetic A/B simulation reproducibility.
Safe-apply workflow implemented: canary (1% traffic), shadow trial, staged promotion (1%, 5%, 25%, 100%) with automated rollback triggers.
Console integration: one-click preview of estimated monthly cost savings and expected hit-rate impact for each suggestion.
Playbook documented with rollback thresholds, incident runbook, and post-rollout validation checklist.
Automated test coverage: unit tests for forecaster, integration tests for simulator, e2e regression test for safe-apply flow.
decisions: Use hybrid forecaster: exponential smoothing for short-term prefix volatility + Bayesian prior informed by sampled sessions to avoid overfitting.
TTL suggestions bounded by configurable min/max per-prefix and a global safety floor to prevent immediate mass misses.
Key canonization rules will be opt-in per-prefix via metadata flag; default behavior is conservative (no aggressive canonicalization).
Batching-aware prefetch only enabled when median request size and expected latency benefit exceed configured thresholds to prevent increased token churn.
rollout_plan: 1) Offline: Run simulator against 14 days of production trace to produce candidate suggestions. 2) Shadow probe: Apply suggestions in shadow mode for selected regions/prefixes for 48h. 3) Canary: Apply to 1% traffic with full telemetry and automatic rollback gates for 24h. 4) Staged promotion: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 6h observation windows. 5) Full apply: apply to remaining traffic and monitor 72h. Rollback triggers: hit-rate drop > 3% relative to baseline for a prefix group OR 99.9th percentile tail latency regression > 5% OR increase in error rate > 0.2%.
telemetry: Token compute cost delta (estimated and observed)
Cache miss storm detector (spike in miss rate across prefixes)
Rollout gating events and automatic rollback logs
implementation_notes: Forecaster should be implemented in Rust for low-latency inline evaluation; batch evaluation can run in Python jobs for richer priors. Simulator will reuse existing cost model from cost-service with an added uncertainty band. Key canonization table kept in config-store with feature flag gating. All changes must include a dry-run mode that emits simulated telemetry to Console.
test_plan: Unit tests for forecaster statistical properties and cold-start behavior
Replay-based regression tests using golden traces and fuzzed variants
Integration test: safe-apply flow with fake traffic generator and injected latency/miss anomalies
Canary validation harness that automatically triggers rollback when thresholds are exceeded
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: cascading cache misses if TTL increases are too large. Mitigation: TTL gradualizer with small step sizes and global safety floor.
Risk: mis-canonicalization losing user-specific signals. Mitigation: opt-in per-prefix rules and explicit exception lists; require PM approval for each prefix with user-affinity.
Risk: inaccurate simulator assumptions. Mitigation: conservative uncertainty margins and mandatory shadow probe before canary.
dependencies_notes: Depends on cost-service updated API for uncertainty bands (ENG-204801) and Console rollout hooks (ENG-864201). Also requires admission from product QA for prefixes flagged as customer-sensitive.
